In detail

A small, mostly institutional and residential district best known for the newly built (2022) 'green' Tibaldi–Università Bocconi railway station serving the nearby Bocconi campus. No documented safety concerns found — a calm, university-adjacent transit node.

Frequently asked questions

Is Tibaldi safe?

Wandroz rates Tibaldi in Milan as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Milan. That rating rests on an area-level review that reached no traveller-relevant reporting specific to Tibaldi — no incidents, no recurring problems, nothing documented either way — read together with the character of the area. It is not a positive finding of safety: an absence of reporting is weaker evidence than the sourced ratings elsewhere on this map, and it is marked as such wherever it appears.

What was checked for Tibaldi?

The same area-level review every other neighbourhood on the Milan map gets: local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist, searched for this specific area. Tibaldi returned nothing traveller-relevant, which is common for smaller administrative areas without a press profile of their own. Where a review does return something, the sources are named on the area's page.

Is Tibaldi a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Nothing documented argues against it. For a stay, weigh that against the areas on the Milan map whose ratings are backed by named sources, and check recent reviews for the specific street. You can search accommodation already scoped to this area using the Booking.com link on this page.
